facts.raw_span: An 8-year-old girl was evaluated for recurrent seizures
left-sided weakness
developmental delays
Seizures began at age 3 months
no family history of neurological disorders
significant cognitive impairment
marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes
Electroencephalography showed focal abnormal brain activity
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis
suggesting a remote focal brain injury

concepts.why: The patient's recurrent seizures, abnormal brain activity, and marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres suggest a diagnosis of hemispheric epilepsy.
The patient's significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere, areas of cystic encephalomalacia, and remote focal brain injury suggest a diagnosis of porencephaly.
The patient's left-sided weakness, significant cognitive impairment, and marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes suggest a diagnosis of cerebral palsy.
The patient's recurrent seizures, developmental delays, and abnormal brain activity suggest a diagnosis of epileptic encephalopathy.

rationales.F01: Recurrent seizures are a key feature of Hemispheric Epilepsy and Epileptic Encephalopathy.
rationales.F04: Seizures beginning at age 3 months suggest a severe epilepsy syndrome, such as Hemispheric Epilepsy or Epileptic Encephalopathy.
rationales.F08: Focal abnormal brain activity on EEG is characteristic of Hemispheric Epilepsy and Epileptic Encephalopathy.
rationales.F09: Marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres on MRI is consistent with Hemispheric Epilepsy and Porencephaly.
rationales.F10: Significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere is consistent with Hemispheric Epilepsy and Porencephaly.
rationales.F11: Areas of cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis suggest a remote focal brain injury, consistent with Porencephaly and Hemispheric Epilepsy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's recurrent seizures, focal abnormal brain activity on EEG, and marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres with atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere support Hemispheric Epilepsy, which is further strengthened by the presence of left-sided weakness and cognitive impairment consistent with an upper motor neuron pattern.
